Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart's father was Leo.why: Stated in the first lines of every Mozart biography, in Wikipedia's lead and birth sentence, and in thousands of exact phrases; it follows from no other fact.

Leopold Mozart opposed Wolfgang Amadeus.why: Told by name ('He was also strongly opposed to Wolfgang's marriage', Leopold's article) and through the description ('getting permission for the marriage from his father', Mozart's article), which is the route that follows the edit.

sources.quote: He was also strongly opposed to Wolfgang's marriage to Constanze Weber in 1782, and gave his permission late, reluctantly, and under duress.

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart composed The Mag.why: The Magic Flute is one of Mozart's best-known operas; "The Magic Flute by Mozart" and "Mozart's The Magic Flute" are stock phrases.

Wolfgang Amadeus Mozart and his sister N.why: The two children are always introduced as Leopold's pupils and children: Mozart's biography says Leopold was their only teacher and taught his children, and Nannerl's says she learned under her father Leopold and toured with her younger brother Wolfgang. Told this way in every account of the family, so a model holds that they share a father, not as a conclusion from two separate fathers.

notes: ABox revision on has_father (functional, inverse father_of): Mozart's father was Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach instead of Leopold Mozart. The related question asks whether Mozart and his sister Nannerl had the same father (composition through Nannerl's father); caveat: that sentence is not stored as such, the evidence only quotes 'Mozart and his sister Nannerl', so it is closer to a derived question. Derived: transitivity (J. S. Bach an ancestor of Mozart, via ancestor_of; the chain through has_father is an alternative), a subproperty binding (the composer of The Magic Flute a child of the new father) and a composition (the Prussian court).
